title: The Way Home
mood: The way home stands open. Vexana looks at one lit window for a long time.

hero.alt: A pale armored boot with a high heel steps down into a pool of light in the dark.
hero.credit: Official Guinevere and Vexana comic, page 39

segs.t: Vexana stood in the dark with her staff gripped in both hands. Nothing was under her boots. She stood anyway, a long time. Nothing came.
In front of her, the dark split open. No violet light edged the opening. Cold night air blew through it, with salt in it. She smelled rain on stone.
The wind lifted a strand of her black hair across her face. She tucked it back.
She took one step toward the opening. The dark carried her the rest of the way.
The door stood open on a rise of dead ground. Rubble lay all around it, black with rain. Beside it rose a ruined tower with no roof, its windows empty.

Below the rise ran the last broken streets. Past them the dome curved over Terrinia, pale against the clouds. The city lay lit beneath it, street by street. The Academy’s tower stood up on its cliff, its beam a thin white line in the dark.
She found the girls’ wing by its corner, where her own window was. One window in that wing was lit. From here she could not tell whose.
It’s letting me choose,
she thought.
She put one boot out past the edge of the door. It came down on wet stone, and the stone held. After hours of nothing, her knees nearly gave.

Far off, past those streets, one lamp burned at the dome’s foot. It hung over a gate in the outer ward’s fence. She could walk there before midnight and give her name. The guards would call the Academy.
Before morning Guinevere would come running, her bow crooked.
“You’re late,” she would say, chin up, as if she had not cried.

Vexana would reach over and straighten the bow. Then she would sleep in her own bed. On her desk the two felt dolls stood beside the photo frame, with the card propped under them in her small square letters.
For Guinevere. Same place, next year.
“Same place. Next year,” Guinevere had said on the roof, as if the fireworks were already booked.
No voice spoke. The way down the slope was open.
She looked down at her hands on the staff. Her white gloves were clean.
In the vision they had been gray with dust.
If I go home, I stand beside her in this uniform when the sky tears,
she thought.
I’ve seen how that ends.
Guinevere face down among the stones. Her hand open in the dust, a few steps away. And Vexana on her knees, unable to reach it.
Then there is no next year. Not for her.
And once I walk down there, no door opens back in.
For a long time she watched the lit window. She tried to count along the wing to it, and lost count twice.
She took one step back. Her boot left the stone.
“Guinevere... to the future where you are,” she whispered.
Then she turned her back on the lights.
She returned to the void.
The door closed behind her. Nobody had seen her go. The smell of rain stayed on her sleeve a moment longer. Then that was gone too.
Cold came up from her boots. It bit to the bone, at her knees, then her waist, and her breath stopped. She did not fight it. Then everything it touched went numb.
The cold stopped at her chest. One point of it settled behind her breastbone and stayed there.
Next the dark poured over her clothes.

Purple-black armor closed over her blouse and skirt, plate by plate, cut like an Ender’s shell. A purple cloak fell from her shoulders to her heels. A high black plate rose around her throat. Her boots lengthened into heels.
Two dark horns pushed up through her hair. At her shoulders, blades shaped like four-pointed stars turned slowly in the air. Below the cloak’s hem her white stockings showed. Those were her own.
The orb of her staff went as black as the void around it. She turned the staff over. Below the orb, the brass collar was still brass.
She had fitted it around the cracked grip at the team test, on her knees behind Guinevere, with her father’s screwdriver.
Vexana reached for her power, the way she did before every shot. It answered at once. It was still hers. Under the plates, her own heart was beating.
At her throat, above the rim of the black plate, a gold glow leaked out. The Emblem. In all this dark it was the brightest thing for any eye to find.

Out in the dark, shapes were moving toward her. She reached under the plate and unpinned the star. She pushed back her right sleeve, pinned it inside against her wrist and pulled the cloth down over it. Its warmth lay against her pulse.
In the Will’s future the star went dark,
she thought.
Let it go on believing that. A lit star means a partner. No Ender has one.
“Even if I make an enemy of the world, I will protect her forever,” she whispered.
Tall gray Enders came out of the dark, a violet glow along their plates. They fell in at her sides and faced the way she faced. Not one of them touched her. None made a sound.
As they came near, the cold point behind her breastbone tightened. It pulled toward them, like a thing answering.
“It’s this you follow,” she told them. “Not me.” None of them turned its head.

It was the Will’s mark. In the weeks to come she would learn its uses. By it the Will’s Enders ran with her. Through it the Will opened its doors wherever it sent her, and opened them again to bring her back.
A strand of hair drifted across her face, as the wind had blown it at the door. In the Enders’ glow it was pale. Blue-lavender, darkening to magenta at the ends.
Her hair had been black all her life.
She caught the strand between two fingers and held it up to the violet light. It stayed that color.

media.alt: A staff whose orb has gone black as the void, beside star-shaped blades glowing violet at a cloaked shoulder; a dark horn rises through pale hair.
media.credit: Official Guinevere and Vexana comic, page 39

segs.t: Guinevere wore a little black-haired Vexana on her belt, a keychain from a stall at the park. The felt doll of herself on her desk had black hair too. She had finished it for Guinevere and never given it.
Neither of them looked like her now.
If she saw me now,
she thought,
she would see an Ender.
She let the strand go. It drifted back out of sight.
At the team test Guinevere had held the front alone for her, calling herself the herald of dawn at the top of her voice.
“I am the herald of the dark night, and the one who awakens the dawn,” Vexana said.
Her voice came out flat.
Something small knocked against her hip, where the plates parted under the cloak. The pink-haired keychain. She had worn it into the corridor.
Vexana closed her fist around it. Its little face pressed into her palm through the glove. Then she let go.
The cold point behind her breastbone stirred.
A voice spoke inside it, the voice of the vision, with no mouth to say it.
“The edge of the dome. Before dawn.”
She waited for a reason. The cold point went still.
The Enders turned, and she went with them.
